title: Stripped-down Flowsheet: Compact perf comparison prototype for model vs route
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a compact, low-noise prototype (desktop-first) that lets operators compare per-model and per-route performance side-by-side in a single flowsheet. This view is intended for fast diagnostics and A/B rollout analysis: triage latency regressions, spot-high-cost routes, and validate canary behavior without leaving the console. The flowsheet is intentionally stripped of heavy chrome—small multiples, consistent time windows, and a single shared time brush allow quick visual comparison.

Primary user stories: 
- As an Ops engineer, I can compare p50/p95/p99 latency for two routes or models across the same time window so I can determine whether a recent rollout impacted tail latency.
- As a Platform PM, I can overlay token-cost and throughput trends to assess whether a spike in latency corresponds to cost increases or higher token counts.
- As an SRE, I can switch each pane between model and route context and pin a baseline model for direct delta calculations.

Prototype highlights (high level):
- Flowsheet layout: 3-column grid (compact sparklines + mini-violin + waterfall per column). Each column represents a chosen subject (model A, model B, route / path).
- Shared time brush: selecting a time range updates all columns and exposes a focused microtraces panel at the bottom.
- Compact metric band above each column with p50/p95/p99 and requests/sec. Values are inline with micro sparklines.
- Token waterfall: compact stacked waterfall for token distribution (prompt, generation, post-process) with avg tokens per request and 95th token count.
- Latency violin: lightweight violin to show latency distribution over the selected brush; overlaid median line and a p99 marker.
- Throughput histogram: small bar chart showing requests per minute; heatmap tint to indicate cost-per-minute (higher cost = warmer tint).
- Cost overlay toggle: when on, a thin area chart overlays the latency sparkline to show token-cost correlation; when off, flowsheet reverts to minimal footprint for quick scanning.
- Rollout integration: each column header includes a rollout badge showing active rollout name, traffic percent, and a small canary timeline dot. Clicking opens rollout actions (Pin baseline, Rollback, Increase traffic).
- Interaction patterns: hover-to-compare (shows delta between two selected columns), keyboard accessible time brush, and lightweight animation for transitions (200ms).

Why different from existing canvases: This prototype trades comprehensive exploration for rapid side-by-side comparison and rollout-aware actions. Rather than large canvases with many widgets, the flowsheet focuses on immediate signal comparison and decision-enabled controls in the header.

Artifacts: Figma prototype, Confluence PRD, example telemetry dataset used for the demo, and a short screencast enumerating the happy path tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Design comps: Figma file with desktop flowsheet + responsive collapse state for tablet (links in attachments)
Three column modes implemented in prototype: model vs model, route vs route, model vs route
Shared time brush updates all columns with <250ms UI feedback in prototype playback
Token waterfall and latency violin are present and show correct p50/p95/p99 markers for the demo dataset
Rollout header actions wired to simulated rollout metadata and present correct traffic percentages
Cost overlay toggle visually distinguishes cost signal and does not block latency sparkline readability
Accessibility: keyboard-only ability to move time brush and compare two columns using focus state
design_notes: Use 3:1 horizontal compression for sparklines vs main mini-chart to keep column widths shallow
Violin chart must be optimized for narrow widths — approximate kernel density using quantile bands if full KDE is too noisy
Token waterfall stacked segments should be normalized to column width; show raw token counts on hover only
Consider using dashed stroke for p99 to maintain visual hierarchy against median and p95
When cost overlay toggled on, use 50% opacity area fill and a separate y-axis label 'estimated $/min'
Rollout badge color protocol: green = stable > 90% traffic, amber = partial < 90% and > 0, red = failing / rollback suggested
Microtraces panel should stream in recent 200 traces for the time brush selection to avoid long loading times
comments: 2025-02-13 - Asha Patel: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focus is on comparison-first layout. Requesting Early Eng run: can we get feedback on viability of violin + waterfall in 280px columns?

2025-02-14 - Jordan Kim (Eng): Quick pass — violin acceptable if approximated via quantiles. Concern: token waterfall stacking may be expensive for live streams; suggest pre-aggregating in backend or using sample windows.
2025-02-15 - Miguel Torres (PM): Love the shared time brush. Please add a 'pin baseline' UX in the header so we can lock a canonical model for rolling deltas.
2025-02-17 - Lena Schreiber (Design): Updated comps with pin baseline and compact action menu. Reduced animation to 150-200ms. Added keyboard focus state for brush handles.

2025-02-19 - Usability review with 3 engineers: Positive for quick triage. Action items: (1) make p99 marker more prominent on low-variance models, (2) add explicit chart legend toggles for cost overlay, (3) ensure vertical stacking order remains consistent across columns.
2025-02-20 - Asha Patel: Preparing handoff doc for frontend. Attached PR points to sample API shape for pre-aggregated metrics. Ready for Eng In Review.
